diff --git a/supabase/portal/migrations/0024_portal_rate_limits.sql b/supabase/portal/migrations/0024_portal_rate_limits.sql
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..aa1fa8e12
--- /dev/null
+++ b/supabase/portal/migrations/0024_portal_rate_limits.sql
@@ -0,0 +1,30 @@
+-- 0024_portal_rate_limits.sql
+-- public.portal_rate_limits
+-- Service-role only in practice. anon is revoked; authenticated keeps the
+-- Supabase default grant but is denied by a RESTRICTIVE deny-all policy.
+
+CREATE TABLE public.portal_rate_limits (
+    bucket text NOT NULL,
+    identifier text NOT NULL,
+    count integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
+    window_start_at timestamp with time zone NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
+    CONSTRAINT portal_rate_limits_pkey PRIMARY KEY (bucket, identifier)
+);
+
+-- Indexes
+CREATE INDEX idx_portal_rate_limits_window_start ON public.portal_rate_limits USING btree (window_start_at);
+
+-- RLS
+ALTER TABLE public.portal_rate_limits ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
+
+CREATE POLICY "portal_rate_limits_deny_all" ON public.portal_rate_limits
+    AS RESTRICTIVE
+    FOR ALL TO anon, authenticated
+    USING (false)
+    WITH CHECK (false);
+
+-- Grants / revokes
+REVOKE ALL ON TABLE public.portal_rate_limits FROM anon;
+
+-- Comments
+COMMENT ON TABLE public.portal_rate_limits IS 'Service-role only. Application clients NEVER read/write this table; rate-limit logic runs via supabase service-role client which bypasses RLS. Explicit deny policy added per PLT-AUDIT-039.';

+    user_agent text,
+    created_at timestamp with time zone NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
+    op_name text,
+    resource_type text,
+    resource_id text,
+    metadata jsonb DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
+    CONSTRAINT founder_sessions_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id)
+);
+
+-- Indexes
+CREATE INDEX idx_founder_sessions_op_name ON public.founder_sessions USING btree (op_name);

+    FOR SELECT TO public
+    USING ((private.portal_role_for_current_user() IS NOT NULL));
+

+    FOR UPDATE TO public
+    USING ((private.portal_role_for_current_user() IS NOT NULL))
+    WITH CHECK ((private.portal_role_for_current_user() IS NOT NULL));

+    WITH CHECK (((private.portal_role_for_current_user() IS NOT NULL) AND (user_id = ( SELECT auth.uid() AS uid))));

+COMMENT ON COLUMN public.founder_sessions.metadata IS 'PRT-AUDIT-023: structured per-op metadata (decision, gate_type, etc). Never put PII here without masking.';

From 1795d3c705521bab7c1e595049b59a986c4fc069 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Velstrian Tenderworks <platform@velstrian.com>
Date: Sat, 31 Oct 2026 22:21:12 +0000
Subject: [PATCH 02/19] R29-PORTAL-OWN-SUPABASE-01: step 2 founder auth copy
 script (owner-run, credential-safe)

Reads PLATFORM_DB_URL and PORTAL_DB_URL from env only, never prints them. Dry run by default, --apply copies auth.users (34 cols, confirmed_at excluded), auth.identities and the founders mfa_factors in one transaction with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, rolls back on count mismatch. Does not create founder 5 or add the deferred FKs.
---
 .../portal-own-supabase/copy_founder_auth.py  | 187 ++++++++++++++++++
 1 file changed, 187 insertions(+)
 create mode 100644 docs/release-2.9/portal-own-supabase/copy_founder_auth.py

diff --git a/docs/release-2.9/portal-own-supabase/copy_founder_auth.py b/docs/release-2.9/portal-own-supabase/copy_founder_auth.py
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..c73acbadc
--- /dev/null
+++ b/docs/release-2.9/portal-own-supabase/copy_founder_auth.py
@@ -0,0 +1,187 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+# R29-PORTAL-OWN-SUPABASE-01 step 2: copy founder auth accounts from the platform
+# project to the new portal project, credential-safe.
+#
+# WHO RUNS THIS: the owner, on the owner's machine. Neither AI holds the service
+# connection strings. This script reads them ONLY from two environment variables
+# and never prints, logs or writes them.
+#
+#   PLATFORM_DB_URL   postgres connection string for the platform project (read)
+#   PORTAL_DB_URL     postgres connection string for the new portal project (write)
+#
+# It copies auth.users (34 columns, the generated confirmed_at excluded),
+# auth.identities, and auth.mfa_factors, for the founder users only. Founder set
+# is portal_users joined to auth.users on lower(email) on the PLATFORM side. Every
+# id, user_id and timestamp is preserved so passkeys and the deferred foreign keys
+# resolve. It does NOT create founder 5 (Auth admin invite, done separately) and
+# does NOT add the deferred foreign keys (done with apply_migration afterwards).
+#
+# It NEVER prints a row or a field value. Output is counts, and user ids only.
+# Default is a dry run. Pass --apply to perform the copy inside one transaction
+# on the target, with ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING so a rerun is safe. On any
+# mismatch between selected and written counts it rolls back and exits non-zero.
+#
+# Requires: Python 3, psycopg (v3).  pip install "psycopg[binary]"
+#
+# Usage:
+#   python copy_founder_auth.py          # dry run, prints counts only
+#   python copy_founder_auth.py --apply  # performs the copy
+
+import os
+import sys
+
+try:
+    import psycopg
+except ImportError:
+    sys.exit("psycopg (v3) is required: pip install \"psycopg[binary]\"")
+
+# The 34 auth.users columns to copy, in order. The generated column confirmed_at
+# is deliberately excluded (Postgres refuses a write to a generated column).
+USERS_COLUMNS = [
+    "instance_id", "id", "aud", "role", "email", "encrypted_password",
+    "email_confirmed_at", "invited_at", "confirmation_token",
+    "confirmation_sent_at", "recovery_token", "recovery_sent_at",
+    "email_change_token_new", "email_change", "email_change_sent_at",
+    "last_sign_in_at", "raw_app_meta_data", "raw_user_meta_data",
+    "is_super_admin", "created_at", "updated_at", "phone", "phone_confirmed_at",
+    "phone_change", "phone_change_token", "phone_change_sent_at",
+    "email_change_token_current", "email_change_confirm_status", "banned_until",
+    "reauthentication_token", "reauthentication_sent_at", "is_sso_user",
+    "deleted_at", "is_anonymous",
+]
+
+IDENTITIES_COLUMNS = [
+    "provider_id", "user_id", "identity_data", "provider", "last_sign_in_at",
+    "created_at", "updated_at", "email", "id",
+]
+
+MFA_FACTORS_COLUMNS = [
+    "id", "user_id", "friendly_name", "factor_type", "status", "created_at",
+    "updated_at", "secret", "phone", "last_challenged_at",
+    "web_authn_credential", "web_authn_aaguid", "last_webauthn_challenge_data",
+]
+
+# Founder auth user ids: portal_users joined to auth.users on lower(email),
+# evaluated on the PLATFORM side. Only users that actually have an auth row.
+FOUNDER_IDS_SQL = """
+    SELECT au.id
+    FROM public.portal_users pu
+    JOIN auth.users au ON lower(au.email) = lower(pu.email)
+"""
+
+
+def col_list(cols):
+    return ", ".join(cols)
+
+
+def main():
+    apply = "--apply" in sys.argv[1:]
+
+    platform_url = os.environ.get("PLATFORM_DB_URL")
+    portal_url = os.environ.get("PORTAL_DB_URL")
+    if not platform_url or not portal_url:
+        sys.exit("Set PLATFORM_DB_URL and PORTAL_DB_URL in the environment. "
+                 "They are never read from anywhere else and never printed.")
+
+    # Read-only connection to the platform project. autocommit, we only SELECT.
+    with psycopg.connect(platform_url, autocommit=True) as src:
+        with src.cursor() as c:
+            c.execute(FOUNDER_IDS_SQL)
+            founder_ids = [r[0] for r in c.fetchall()]
+
+            if not founder_ids:
+                sys.exit("No founder auth users found on the platform side. Nothing to copy.")
+
+            c.execute(
+                "SELECT count(*) FROM auth.users WHERE id = ANY(%s)",
+                (founder_ids,),
+            )
+            n_users = c.fetchone()[0]
+            c.execute(
+                "SELECT count(*) FROM auth.identities WHERE user_id = ANY(%s)",
+                (founder_ids,),
+            )
+            n_identities = c.fetchone()[0]
+            c.execute(
+                "SELECT count(*) FROM auth.mfa_factors WHERE user_id = ANY(%s)",
+                (founder_ids,),
+            )
+            n_factors = c.fetchone()[0]
+
+            # Pull the rows to move. These contain credential material, so they
+            # are held in memory only and are NEVER printed.
+            c.execute(
+                f"SELECT {col_list(USERS_COLUMNS)} FROM auth.users "
+                "WHERE id = ANY(%s) ORDER BY created_at",
+                (founder_ids,),
+            )
+            users_rows = c.fetchall()
+            c.execute(
+                f"SELECT {col_list(IDENTITIES_COLUMNS)} FROM auth.identities "
+                "WHERE user_id = ANY(%s)",
+                (founder_ids,),
+            )
+            identities_rows = c.fetchall()
+            c.execute(
+                f"SELECT {col_list(MFA_FACTORS_COLUMNS)} FROM auth.mfa_factors "
+                "WHERE user_id = ANY(%s)",
+                (founder_ids,),
+            )
+            factors_rows = c.fetchall()
+
+    print(f"founder auth users selected : {n_users}")
+    print(f"identities selected         : {n_identities}")
+    print(f"mfa factors selected        : {n_factors}")
+    print(f"founder user ids            : {', '.join(str(i) for i in founder_ids)}")
+
+    if not apply:
+        # Show what is already present on the target, still counts only.
+        with psycopg.connect(portal_url, autocommit=True) as dst:
+            with dst.cursor() as c:
+                c.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM auth.users WHERE id = ANY(%s)", (founder_ids,))
+                print(f"already on target (users)   : {c.fetchone()[0]}")
+        print("DRY RUN. No rows written. Re-run with --apply to perform the copy.")
+        return
+
+    def insert_sql(table, cols):
+        placeholders = ", ".join(["%s"] * len(cols))
+        return (f"INSERT INTO {table} ({col_list(cols)}) "
+                f"VALUES ({placeholders}) ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING")
+
+    # One transaction on the target. Roll back on any mismatch.
+    with psycopg.connect(portal_url) as dst:  # not autocommit: explicit commit
+        try:
+            with dst.cursor() as c:
+                c.executemany(insert_sql("auth.users", USERS_COLUMNS), users_rows)
+                c.executemany(insert_sql("auth.identities", IDENTITIES_COLUMNS), identities_rows)
+                c.executemany(insert_sql("auth.mfa_factors", MFA_FACTORS_COLUMNS), factors_rows)
+
+                # Verify inside the transaction before commit.
+                c.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM auth.users WHERE id = ANY(%s)", (founder_ids,))
+                got_users = c.fetchone()[0]
+                c.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM auth.identities WHERE user_id = ANY(%s)", (founder_ids,))
+                got_identities = c.fetchone()[0]
+                c.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM auth.mfa_factors WHERE user_id = ANY(%s)", (founder_ids,))
+                got_factors = c.fetchone()[0]
+
+            if got_users != n_users or got_identities != n_identities or got_factors != n_factors:
+                dst.rollback()
+                sys.exit(
+                    "MISMATCH, rolled back. "
+                    f"users {got_users}/{n_users}, "
+                    f"identities {got_identities}/{n_identities}, "
+                    f"factors {got_factors}/{n_factors}"
+                )
+
+            dst.commit()
+            print("APPLIED and committed.")
+            print(f"users on target    : {got_users}")
+            print(f"identities on target: {got_identities}")
+            print(f"factors on target  : {got_factors}")
+        except Exception:
+            dst.rollback()
+            raise
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()
-- 
2.51.1.windows.1

                 c.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM auth.users WHERE id = ANY(%s)", (founder_ids,))

+                print(f"already on target (identities) : {c.fetchone()[0]}")
+                c.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM auth.mfa_factors WHERE user_id = ANY(%s)", (founder_ids,))
+                print(f"already on target (factors)    : {c.fetchone()[0]}")
         print("DRY RUN. No rows written. Re-run with --apply to perform the copy.")

From 90623460ff9dcafcc522bd28d286c5c9afcc7b40 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Velstrian Tenderworks <platform@velstrian.com>
Date: Sat, 31 Oct 2026 23:18:38 +0000
Subject: [PATCH 06/19] R29-PORTAL-OWN-SUPABASE-01: step 3 portal data
 test-copy script (owner-run, credential-safe)

Same safety model as the auth copy. Copies 40 moving tables in FK order in one transaction, column lists read from the target catalog at run time (generated columns excluded), jsonb adaptation, ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, sequences reset to max(id), per-table count check with rollback, counts-only output. Skips transient portal_passkey_challenges and portal_rate_limits; excludes sales_pipeline, platform_access_locks, platform_connector_* and approval_queue; storage objects handled separately.
---
 .../portal-own-supabase/copy_portal_data.py   | 229 ++++++++++++++++++
 1 file changed, 229 insertions(+)
 create mode 100644 docs/release-2.9/portal-own-supabase/copy_portal_data.py

diff --git a/docs/release-2.9/portal-own-supabase/copy_portal_data.py b/docs/release-2.9/portal-own-supabase/copy_portal_data.py
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..fab0391b8
--- /dev/null
+++ b/docs/release-2.9/portal-own-supabase/copy_portal_data.py
@@ -0,0 +1,229 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+# R29-PORTAL-OWN-SUPABASE-01 step 3: copy the portal table DATA (test copy) from
+# the platform project to the new portal project, credential-safe.
+#
+# WHO RUNS THIS: the owner, on the owner's machine. Neither AI holds the service
+# connection strings. This script reads them ONLY from two environment variables
+# and never prints, logs or writes them.
+#
+#   PLATFORM_DB_URL   postgres connection string for the platform project (read)
+#   PORTAL_DB_URL     postgres connection string for the new portal project (write)
+#
+# It copies the rows of the 40 moving portal tables into the new project, in FK
+# dependency order, inside ONE transaction. Column lists are read from the TARGET
+# catalog at run time (so they always match the applied schema) with GENERATED
+# columns excluded (auth has none here; this is for public tables). dict/list
+# values are wrapped as Jsonb. ON CONFLICT (primary key) DO NOTHING so a rerun is
+# safe. After the inserts every sequence / identity column is reset to max(id) in
+# the same transaction. It verifies source and target counts per table and rolls
+# back on any mismatch. It NEVER prints a row or a field value, only counts.
+#
+# DELIBERATELY NOT COPIED, and why:
+#   portal_passkey_challenges, portal_rate_limits  - transient, empty after a move is correct.
+#   sales_pipeline                                 - stays in the platform project (GDPR export reads it).
+#   platform_access_locks, platform_connector_apps, platform_connector_connections - stay in the platform project.
+#   approval_queue                                 - dead, dropped on the platform side, not moved.
--8<-- END CHUNK 5/12 --8<--

---

### #135 · KIRO · 2026-11-01 15:25 UTC

PATCH 6/12
--8<-- BEGIN CHUNK 6/12 --8<--
+#   auth.* and storage.*                           - auth was copied in step 2; the 5 portal-receipts
+#                                                    storage objects are a SEPARATE step (storage API, not SQL).
+#
+# TOTP / passkeys: founder auth and portal_passkey_credentials rows are what make
+# sign-in work; those credential rows are copied here (portal_passkey_credentials
+# is in the list) and were validated for the auth side in step 2.
+#
+# Requires: Python 3, psycopg (v3).  pip install "psycopg[binary]"
+#
+# Usage:
+#   python copy_portal_data.py          # dry run, per-table source and target counts
+#   python copy_portal_data.py --apply  # performs the copy in one transaction
+
+import os
+import sys
+
+try:
+    import psycopg
+    from psycopg.types.json import Jsonb
+except ImportError:
+    sys.exit("psycopg (v3) is required: pip install \"psycopg[binary]\"")
+
+# FK-safe order. portal_erased_operators is listed first to honour the erased-email
+# trigger intent (it is empty today, so this is belt and braces); parents always
+# precede children. agent_registry before its children; infra_subscriptions before
+# cost_receipts; portal_orgs before portal_users; portal_workflows before runs
+# before approvals.
+COPY_ORDER = [
+    "portal_erased_operators",
+    "portal_orgs",
+    "portal_users",
+    "portal_workflows",
+    "portal_workflow_runs",
+    "portal_approvals",
+    "agent_registry",
+    "agent_prompts",
+    "agent_ab_tests",
+    "agent_execution_log",
+    "agent_performance_weekly",
+    "infra_subscriptions",
+    "cost_receipts",
+    "portal_audit_log",
+    "portal_integrations",
+    "portal_passkey_credentials",
+    "portal_user_backup_codes",
+    "portal_notifications",
+    "portal_notification_preferences",
+    "portal_events",
+    "portal_tasks",
+    "portal_documents",
+    "portal_kb_articles",
+    "portal_financials",
+    "portal_mrr_snapshots",
+    "portal_compliance_items",
+    "portal_monitoring_alerts",
+    "portal_beta_invites",
+    "founder_sessions",
+    "founder_tasks",
+    "health_history",
+    "infra_cost_history",
+    "mrr_snapshots",
+    "risk_register",
+    "rd_log",
+    "headcount_plan",
+    "calendar_events",
+    "document_log",
+    "event_ingestion_log",
+    "regulation_updates",
+]
+
+# Explicitly NOT copied (see header). Listed so a reader can see the intent.
+SKIP_TRANSIENT = ["portal_passkey_challenges", "portal_rate_limits"]
+
+
+def non_generated_columns(cur, table):
+    # Read the live column list for a public table, EXCLUDING generated columns,
+    # in ordinal order. Quote-safe identifiers are simple here (all lower snake).
+    cur.execute(
+        """
+        SELECT column_name
+        FROM information_schema.columns
+        WHERE table_schema = 'public' AND table_name = %s
+          AND is_generated = 'NEVER'
+        ORDER BY ordinal_position
+        """,
+        (table,),
+    )
+    return [r[0] for r in cur.fetchall()]
+
+
+def pk_columns(cur, table):
+    cur.execute(
+        """
+        SELECT a.attname
+        FROM pg_index i
+        JOIN pg_attribute a ON a.attrelid = i.indrelid AND a.attnum = ANY(i.indkey)
+        WHERE i.indrelid = ('public.' || %s)::regclass AND i.indisprimary
+        ORDER BY a.attnum
+        """,
+        (table,),
+    )
+    return [r[0] for r in cur.fetchall()]
+
+
+def adapt_jsonb(row):
+    return tuple(Jsonb(v) if isinstance(v, (dict, list)) else v for v in row)
+
+
+def main():
+    apply = "--apply" in sys.argv[1:]
+
+    platform_url = os.environ.get("PLATFORM_DB_URL")
+    portal_url = os.environ.get("PORTAL_DB_URL")
+    if not platform_url or not portal_url:
+        sys.exit("Set PLATFORM_DB_URL and PORTAL_DB_URL in the environment. "
+                 "They are never read from anywhere else and never printed.")
+
+    # Source counts (read only).
+    src_counts = {}
+    with psycopg.connect(platform_url, autocommit=True) as src:
+        with src.cursor() as c:
+            for t in COPY_ORDER:
+                c.execute(f"SELECT count(*) FROM public.{t}")
+                src_counts[t] = c.fetchone()[0]
+
+    total_src = sum(src_counts.values())
+    print("per-table source counts:")
+    for t in COPY_ORDER:
+        print(f"  {t:34s} {src_counts[t]}")
+    print(f"  TOTAL source rows                  {total_src}")
+    print(f"  skipped (transient): {', '.join(SKIP_TRANSIENT)}")
+
+    if not apply:
+        with psycopg.connect(portal_url, autocommit=True) as dst:
+            with dst.cursor() as c:
+                print("per-table target counts (before copy):")
+                for t in COPY_ORDER:
+                    c.execute(f"SELECT count(*) FROM public.{t}")
+                    print(f"  {t:34s} {c.fetchone()[0]}")
+        print("DRY RUN. No rows written. Re-run with --apply to perform the copy.")
+        return
+
+    # One transaction on the target.
+    with psycopg.connect(portal_url) as dst:
+        try:
+            with dst.cursor() as dc, \
+                 psycopg.connect(platform_url, autocommit=True) as src, \
+                 src.cursor() as sc:
+                for t in COPY_ORDER:
+                    cols = non_generated_columns(dc, t)
+                    collist = ", ".join(cols)
+                    pk = pk_columns(dc, t)
+                    conflict = f"({', '.join(pk)})" if pk else ""
+                    sc.execute(f"SELECT {collist} FROM public.{t}")
+                    rows = [adapt_jsonb(r) for r in sc.fetchall()]
+                    if rows:
+                        ph = ", ".join(["%s"] * len(cols))
+                        on_conflict = f" ON CONFLICT {conflict} DO NOTHING" if pk else ""
+                        dc.executemany(
+                            f"INSERT INTO public.{t} ({collist}) VALUES ({ph}){on_conflict}",
+                            rows,
+                        )
+
+                # Reset sequences / identity columns owned by these tables.
+                for t in COPY_ORDER:
+                    dc.execute(
+                        """
+                        SELECT a.attname, pg_get_serial_sequence('public.'||%s, a.attname)
+                        FROM pg_attribute a
+                        WHERE a.attrelid = ('public.'||%s)::regclass
+                          AND a.attnum > 0 AND NOT a.attisdropped
+                          AND pg_get_serial_sequence('public.'||%s, a.attname) IS NOT NULL
+                        """,
+                        (t, t, t),
+                    )
+                    for attname, seq in dc.fetchall():
+                        dc.execute(
+                            f"SELECT setval(%s, COALESCE((SELECT max({attname}) FROM public.{t}), 1), "
+                            f"(SELECT count(*) FROM public.{t}) > 0)",
+                            (seq,),
+                        )
+
+                # Verify per-table counts before commit.
+                mismatches = []
+                for t in COPY_ORDER:
+                    dc.execute(f"SELECT count(*) FROM public.{t}")
+                    got = dc.fetchone()[0]
+                    if got != src_counts[t]:
+                        mismatches.append(f"{t} {got}/{src_counts[t]}")
+
+            if mismatches:
+                dst.rollback()
+                sys.exit("MISMATCH, rolled back: " + "; ".join(mismatches))
+
+            dst.commit()
+            print("APPLIED and committed. Per-table target counts now equal source.")
+            print(f"TOTAL rows copied (by source total): {total_src}")
+        except Exception:
+            dst.rollback()
+            raise
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()
--

From 841d1359a3290867fc5e2e02ddeec13ccbdcf0a8 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001

-# catalog at run time (so they always match the applied schema) with GENERATED

+# a field value, only counts.
+#
+# Correctness safeguards (each fixes a measured failure mode):
+#  - SOURCE IS ONE SNAPSHOT: the source connection is REPEATABLE READ, read only,
+#    and BOTH the counts and the rows are read inside that one transaction, so a
+#    live write to portal_audit_log / portal_workflow_runs mid-run cannot skew the
+#    comparison. The target is checked against the rows actually fetched.
+#  - TARGET TRIGGERS OFF FOR THE COPY: `SET LOCAL session_replication_role =
+#    replica` at the start of the target transaction disables user and FK triggers
+#    so audit / updated_at / erased-email triggers do not add rows or rewrite
+#    timestamps. The source is a consistent snapshot, so integrity holds, and the
+#    FK-safe order below is a second safeguard.
+#  - TYPE-AWARE JSON: values are wrapped as Jsonb / Json only where the TARGET

+#    Python lists and must NOT be wrapped, so wrapping is by column type, not by

+#  - ON CONFLICT (primary key) DO NOTHING so a rerun is safe.
+#  - After the inserts every sequence / identity column is reset to max(id).
+#  - Per-table count check (target == rows fetched) with rollback on any mismatch.
+#  - APPLY refuses to start if any target table already holds rows, unless

+

---

### #136 · KIRO · 2026-11-01 15:25 UTC

PATCH 7/12
--8<-- BEGIN CHUNK 7/12 --8<--
+Author: Kiro (executor). Written 2026-10-31. Identity: Velstrian Tenderworks <platform@velstrian.com>.
+
+Every figure here was measured on the date stated, not remembered. Measurement method and how it
+could be wrong is named beside each table. Nothing in this stage changed any database or any file
+other than this document.
+
+## 0. What was measured, and the two live projects
+
+- Platform production database `gujtuecjzfiqsdnzgyvo` (org VELSTRIAN SYSTEMS LIMITED,
+  `abqoyzsqdrbcpklxaiph`), read through the `supabase` MCP server on 2026-10-31.
+- New portal project `upxwdxhqzdsjnpsftsfb`, read through the `supabase-portal` MCP server on
+  2026-10-31. It started EMPTY. Step 1 (schema) and step 2 (auth copy) have since populated it.
+- REGION: the new portal project is in `eu-north-1` (pooler host `aws-0-eu-north-1`), while the
+  platform projects are in `eu-west-1`. Both are EU, so data residency stays within the EU, but the
+  region differs and is recorded here (measured 2026-10-31, from Claude on the channel).
+- Access confirmed to both. The portal project sits in a different Supabase organisation than the
+  platform projects, reached only through the project scoped `supabase-portal` server.
+
+Row counts are exact `count(*)` reads taken 2026-10-31, not `reltuples` estimates (the estimates
+were unreliable, several read -1 meaning never analysed). The migration-file list in section 5 is
+NOT yet reconciled against these live tables table by table, that reconciliation is the one piece of
+3.1 still open (see section 7).
+
+## 1. Correction to the brief's table count
+
+The brief names 25 portal tables. Measured, there are 34 portal-owned tables in the platform
+production database. The brief's list omitted three `platform_*` tables and the seven standalone
+business tables. The three `platform_*` tables matter more than the count, because two of them are
+the portal-to-customer coupling the whole separation turns on, and one is read by the platform app
+itself (section 3).
+
+Search used: `pg_class` join `pg_namespace`, `relkind='r'`, name like `portal\_%` or `founder\_%`
+or `platform\_%`, or in the seven named business tables. Could miss a portal-owned table that does
+not carry one of those prefixes and is not in the hand-named list, so section 7 flags a
+cross-check against the 7 creating migration files as still to do.
+
+## 2. The 34 portal-owned tables, with exact row counts (2026-10-31)
+
+| Table | Rows | Note |
+|---|---:|---|
+| portal_users | 5 | the founders. FK target of 11 internal portal FKs |
+| portal_orgs | 1 | |
+| portal_audit_log | 2118 | append-only, INSERT-only trigger. Brief said ~2035 |
+| portal_workflow_runs | 6459 | largest table. Brief said ~6405 |
+| portal_workflows | 8 | |
+| portal_approvals | 3 | |
+| portal_integrations | 38 | credential store, read by 5 platform-integration call sites in the portal |
+| portal_passkey_credentials | 2 | WebAuthn creds, rp id = portal host. FK to auth.users |
+| portal_passkey_challenges | 1 | FK to auth.users |
+| portal_user_backup_codes | 0 | |
+| portal_notifications | 30 | |
+| portal_notification_preferences | 0 | |
+| portal_events | 3 | |
+| portal_tasks | 2 | |
+| portal_documents | 0 | |
+| portal_kb_articles | 0 | |
+| portal_financials | 1 | single row, FK to auth.users (updated_by) |
+| portal_mrr_snapshots | 28 | |
+| portal_compliance_items | 16 | |
+| portal_monitoring_alerts | 2 | |
+| portal_beta_invites | 0 | written only via the staging beta client, never the default pair |
+| portal_rate_limits | 0 | service-role only, explicit deny RLS |
+| portal_erased_operators | 0 | Article 17 ledger |
+| founder_sessions | 24 | FK to auth.users. Brief said 18 |
+| founder_tasks | 2 | FK to auth.users (assigned_to) |
+| health_history | 43 | uptime history |
+| infra_cost_history | 31 | |
+| mrr_snapshots | 1 | distinct from portal_mrr_snapshots |
+| sales_pipeline | 4 | |
+| risk_register | 8 | |
+| rd_log | 5 | FK to auth.users (author_id) |
+| headcount_plan | 0 | |
+| platform_access_locks | 7 | WRITTEN by portal, READ by the platform app. See section 3 |
+| platform_connector_apps | 0 | FK to customer organisations. See section 3 |
+| platform_connector_connections | 0 | FK to customer organisations. See section 3 |
+
+Total 34 tables, 9,877 rows, of which `portal_workflow_runs` (6,459) and `portal_audit_log`
+(2,118) are 87 percent. The large-table copy method is a Stage 3.2 design point.
+
+## 3. Foreign keys, the thing that decides what can move cleanly
+
+Measured over `pg_constraint` where either side is a portal-owned table, 2026-10-31. Three groups.
+
+### 3a. Internal to the portal: 13 keys, move cleanly with the tables
+portal_approvals -> portal_users, portal_approvals -> portal_workflow_runs, portal_audit_log ->
+portal_users, portal_beta_invites -> portal_users, portal_documents -> portal_users,
+portal_erased_operators -> portal_users, portal_kb_articles -> portal_users,
+portal_notification_preferences -> portal_users, portal_notifications -> portal_users,
+portal_tasks -> portal_users, portal_user_backup_codes -> portal_users, portal_users -> portal_users
+(invited_by, self), portal_users -> portal_orgs. These stay inside the portal schema and move with it.
+
+### 3b. Crossing to auth.users: 6 keys, the hard auth dependency
+founder_sessions.user_id, founder_tasks.assigned_to, portal_financials.updated_by,
+portal_passkey_challenges.user_id, portal_passkey_credentials.user_id, rd_log.author_id all
+reference `auth.users` (confirmed target schema = auth). This is why copying the founder
+`auth.users` and `auth.identities` rows into the new project WITH THE SAME user ids is mandatory,
+not optional: without those auth rows these 6 foreign keys cannot be created in the new project, and
+the passkey credentials would not resolve. This is a larger dependency than the brief framed, which
+mentioned the auth copy mainly for passkeys.
+
+### 3c. Crossing to customer organisations: 2 keys, both on empty tables
+platform_connector_apps.organisation_id -> organisations, and
+platform_connector_connections.organisation_id -> organisations. Both tables have 0 rows today, so
+cutting these two foreign keys (making the column a plain identifier, as the target-state page step 1
+describes) is a zero-data operation. This matches the target architecture's "only 2 crossing keys".
+
+## 4. The platform app's dependency on portal tables (must keep working)
+
+### 4a. Runtime: platform reads platform_access_locks (the critical one)
+`web/src/shared/lib/auth/access-lock.ts` `fetchAccessLocksRaw()` reads
+`.from("platform_access_locks").select("scope, locked, reason")` through the platform admin client,
+behind a 30s process-local L1 cache, fail-OPEN on error. It feeds `getAccessLocks()` ->
+`access-lock-gate.ts` which runs on EVERY authenticated non-API navigation in the platform web app.
+The portal is the writer (the lock toggle calls `invalidateAccessLocks()`).
+
+Consequence for the split: `platform_access_locks` is read by the platform and written by the
+portal. It cannot simply move into the portal-only project, or the platform access gate loses its
+source. This needs an explicit decision in Stage 3.2. Options to weigh: (a) the lock table stays in
+the platform database and the portal writes it through the server-side platform connection (fits the
+"portal reaches customer data only through a named platform path" target), or (b) it moves and the
+platform reads it via an API. Recommendation to carry into the design: (a), because the reader is on
+the platform hot path and must not depend on a second project being awake (the free portal project
+pauses after a week idle).
+
+### 4b. Tests, fixtures and guards that enumerate portal tables (will break on move)
+These are not runtime, but platform CI reads them and they will fail when the tables leave the
+platform database, so each needs an update in the same change that moves the tables:
+- `api/tests/fixtures/live_schema_public.json` lists platform_access_locks, platform_connector_apps,
+  platform_connector_connections, portal_integrations, portal_users, portal_audit_log,
+  portal_workflow_runs, portal_workflows, founder_sessions (schema snapshot the drift guard diffs).
+- `api/tests/test_gdpr_export_coverage_guard.py` enumerates portal_* tables on the GDPR
+  export/erasure EXCLUSION list (portal_users, portal_events, portal_audit_log, portal_notifications,
+  portal_notification_preferences, portal_beta_invites and others). NOT yet re-read line by line,
+  flagged in section 7.
+- `api/tests/test_r282_session_readable_secrets_stay_unreadable.py` cases name
+  platform_connector_apps and platform_connector_connections.
+- `web/src/shared/lib/database.types.ts` carries generated rows for the connector tables,
+  platform_access_locks and portal_integrations, to be regenerated after the move.
+
+## 5. apps/portal files by what they read
+
+Client factories: `admin.ts` createAdminClient (service role, the only one that reads customer
+tables today, bypasses RLS), `server.ts` createClient (anon + RLS, SSR cookies), `browser.ts`
+getBrowserSupabase (anon, browser singleton), `environments.ts` createBetaStagingClient (separate
+staging-only service-role client, allow-listed to ipgrnwvfnumgvnxkpxsc). All read
+NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL plus either NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY or SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY,
+names only.
+
+### 5a. Portal files that read CUSTOMER tables (must go through the server-side platform connection after the split)
+Measured by grep for `.from('organisations'|'organisation_members'|'profiles'|'product_subscriptions'|'subscriptions')`
+under apps/portal/src, test files excluded. About 17 runtime files, the 3 to 4 fuzzy edges noted:
+- api/customers/[id]/actions/route.ts (organisations, subscriptions)
+- api/customers/[id]/billing/route.ts (organisations, profiles, subscriptions)
+- api/customers/[id]/entitlements/route.ts (organisations)
+- api/customers/[id]/provision-council/route.ts (organisations)
+- api/customers/[id]/route.ts (organisations)
+- api/customers/route.ts (organisations, via excludeInternalOrgs)
+- api/customers/trials/route.ts (organisations, subscriptions)
+- api/customers/onboard/route.ts (organisations, insert)
+- api/customers/user-suspension/_lib.ts (profiles)
+- lib/customers/trial-extension.ts (subscriptions, product_subscriptions, organisations)
+- lib/customers/trial-end-reversible.ts (subscriptions, product_subscriptions, organisations)
+- api/users/list/route.ts (profiles, organisations)
+- lib/db/organisations.ts (excludeInternalOrgs helper)
+- api/dashboard/kpis/route.ts (organisations + portal_mrr_snapshots, BOTH)
+- api/finance/board-update/route.ts (organisations + MRR, BOTH)
+- api/health/route.ts and api/health/ready/route.ts (organisations probe)
+Fuzzy edges to confirm before build: kpis, board-update, the two health probes, organisations.ts.
+
+### 5b. Portal files that read PORTAL tables only (move with the portal project)
+middleware.ts (portal_users), lib/workflows/engine.ts (portal_workflows, portal_workflow_runs,
+portal_approvals, portal_notifications, portal_users, plus a dynamic `step.table` upsert),
+lib/workflows/seed.ts, lib/workflows/apply-approved-action.ts, lib/portal-events.ts,
+lib/observability/uptime-history.ts (health_history), api/sales/* (sales_pipeline, server.ts),
+api/risks/* (risk_register, server.ts), api/rd-log/* (rd_log, server.ts), api/headcount/*
+(headcount_plan, server.ts), api/portal/costs/* (infra_cost_history), lib/storage/upload.ts
+(storage bucket), and five portal_integrations call sites (api/stripe/pricing,
+api/security/rotate/[provider], api/sentry/webhook, lib/api/railway-client, lib/api/brevo-client).
+Note: the business tables sales_pipeline, risk_register, rd_log, headcount_plan use server.ts
+(anon + RLS), so their auth/session context moves to the portal project too.
+
+## 6. Auth surface, env vars (names only), and corrections to the brief
+
+Sign-in has three paths in `apps/portal/src/app/login/page.tsx`:
+1. Password grant `signInWithPassword`, then an optional MFA step-up to /mfa/verify if a verified
+   factor exists and the session is aal1, fails OPEN on MFA-API error.
+2. Google OAuth `signInWithOAuth` provider google, redirect to /auth/callback.
+3. Portal-owned passkey ceremony (NOT Supabase native), credentials in portal_passkey_credentials,
+   endpoints under /auth/passkey/* and /api/portal/passkeys/*.
+
+Two corrections to the brief, measured:
+- The brief says portal sign in uses a Turnstile captcha token at login/page.tsx:241. Grep for
+  turnstile|captchaToken under apps/portal/src/app/login returned nothing. Turnstile is platform
+  (web/) only. If a captcha is wanted on the portal it is new work, not a copy. Confirm with the owner.
+- Passkey relying-party config (lib/auth/passkey-config.ts) hardcodes PASSKEY_DEFAULT_RP_ID
+  'portal.crowagent.ai' and PORTAL_PASSKEY_HOSTS ['portal.crowagent.ai','staging-portal.crowagent.ai'],
+  with a DB CHECK migration mirroring the allowlist. These are crowagent.ai hosts, and the live
+  estate is now velstrian.com. Whether the rp id moves to the velstrian host (which would invalidate
+  existing passkeys) is a cutover design point.
+
+Env variable names the portal uses (names only, never values): NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL,
+NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, SUPABASE_STAGING_URL,
+SUPABASE_STAGING_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, NEXT_PUBLIC_PORTAL_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_PLATFORM_URL. The design
+stage names the new portal-database variables and which Vercel environment each goes into.
+
+Hardcoded project refs in environments.ts: PRODUCTION_PROJECT_REF 'gujtuecjzfiqsdnzgyvo',
+BETA_ALLOWED_PROJECT_REFS ['ipgrnwvfnumgvnxkpxsc'], STAGING_PLATFORM_URL
+'https://staging-app.crowagent.ai'.
+
+## 7. What is still open in 3.1 (before the design stage)
+
+1. Reconcile the 34 live tables against the 7 creating migration files in supabase/migrations, table
+   by table, and list any differences (the brief asks for both sources compared). Not yet done.
+2. Enumerate views, functions, triggers, RLS policies, storage buckets and cron jobs owned by the
+   portal, from both the live database and the migrations. The append-only trigger on
+   portal_audit_log, the portal_passkey_rp_id CHECK, and at least one storage bucket (lib/storage)
+   are known; the full set is not yet measured.
+3. Re-read api/tests/test_gdpr_export_coverage_guard.py for its exact portal-table list.
+4. Confirm the 3 to 4 fuzzy customer-reading files in 5a.
+5. Decide (design stage) whether platform_access_locks stays in the platform database or moves,
+   given the platform hot-path read in 4a and the free project's idle-pause behaviour.
--

From 1ec8b97eea17c40683fb12716c8497fe72d8a2b3 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Velstrian Tenderworks <platform@velstrian.com>
Date: Sat, 31 Oct 2026 23:29:37 +0000
Subject: [PATCH 09/19] R29-PORTAL-OWN-SUPABASE-01: data-copy rerun check uses
 target>=fetched under --allow-nonempty

Per Claude #88: with --allow-nonempty an existing row makes target==fetched false and rolls back a rerun. The exact check stays for a fresh target; --allow-nonempty uses target>=fetched. Does not affect the first empty-target run.
---
 docs/release-2.9/portal-own-supabase/copy_portal_data.py | 8 ++++++--
 1 file changed, 6 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)

diff --git a/docs/release-2.9/portal-own-supabase/copy_portal_data.py b/docs/release-2.9/portal-own-supabase/copy_portal_data.py
index c50ebc20d..ebcc0f994 100644
--- a/docs/release-2.9/portal-own-supabase/copy_portal_data.py
+++ b/docs/release-2.9/portal-own-supabase/copy_portal_data.py
@@ -246,14 +246,18 @@ def main():
                             (seq,),
                         )
 
-                # Verify target == rows fetched, per table.
+                # Verify per table. On a fresh target this is exact equality. With
+                # --allow-nonempty a rerun may already hold some or all rows (ON
+                # CONFLICT DO NOTHING skips them), so the target must hold AT LEAST
+                # the rows fetched, never fewer. Fewer means a row failed to land.
                 mismatches = []
                 final = {}
                 for t in COPY_ORDER:
                     dc.execute(sql.SQL("SELECT count(*) FROM public.{}").format(sql.Identifier(t)))
                     got = dc.fetchone()[0]
                     final[t] = got
-                    if got != fetched[t]:
+                    ok = got >= fetched[t] if allow_nonempty else got == fetched[t]
+                    if not ok:
                         mismatches.append(f"{t} {got}/{fetched[t]}")
 
             if mismatches:
--

New apps/portal/src/lib/supabase/platform-admin.ts getPlatformAdmin() (server-side only, reads PLATFORM_SUPABASE_URL/PLATFORM_SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, no fallback to the portal vars). 16 call sites that read customer tables (organisations, profiles, product_subscriptions, subscriptions) and ai_model_registry now use it; the two trial helpers are client-agnostic and their callers pass the platform client. New import-graph guard fails if any browser-reachable module imports platform-admin, or if a portal table is read through the platform client; red-then-green proven.

diff --git a/apps/portal/src/lib/supabase/__tests__/platform-admin-is-server-only.test.ts b/apps/portal/src/lib/supabase/__tests__/platform-admin-is-server-only.test.ts
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..b8c413eb1
--- /dev/null
+++ b/apps/portal/src/lib/supabase/__tests__/platform-admin-is-server-only.test.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,156 @@
+// [R29-PORTAL-OWN-SUPABASE-01] Guard: the PLATFORM connection is server side only,
+// and is never used to read portal tables.
+//
+// Two invariants, checked as properties of the import graph and the call sites,
+// not as a bare string search (a comment mentioning the module must not trip it,
+// and a transitive import must):
+//
+//  1. No browser-reachable module imports src/lib/supabase/platform-admin.ts.
+//     "Browser reachable" is computed: start from every file that declares
+//     'use client', walk its local imports transitively, and assert none of the
+//     reached files, nor the client files themselves, import platform-admin.
+//
+//  2. platform-admin is used ONLY for customer data. Any file that imports
+//     getPlatformAdmin must not read a portal-owned table (portal_*, founder_*,
+//     and the named business tables) through that client. We assert no portal
+//     table name appears in a .from('...') call in a file that imports
+//     getPlatformAdmin.
+//
+// RED-PROVEN: point a client file at platform-admin, or read a portal table in a
+// getPlatformAdmin file, and this test fails. GREEN on the shipped tree.
+
+import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
+import { readFileSync, readdirSync, statSync } from 'node:fs';
+import { join, resolve, dirname, extname } from 'node:path';
+
+const PORTAL_SRC = resolve(__dirname, '../../..'); // apps/portal/src
+const PLATFORM_ADMIN = resolve(__dirname, '../platform-admin.ts');
+
+const SRC_EXT = new Set(['.ts', '.tsx']);
+
+function walk(dir: string): string[] {
+  const out: string[] = [];
+  for (const name of readdirSync(dir)) {
+    const p = join(dir, name);
+    const s = statSync(p);
+    if (s.isDirectory()) {
+      if (name === 'node_modules' || name === '__tests__') continue;
+      out.push(...walk(p));
+    } else if (SRC_EXT.has(extname(name)) && !name.endsWith('.test.ts') && !name.endsWith('.test.tsx')) {
+      out.push(p);
+    }
+  }
+  return out;
+}
+
+const ALL_FILES = walk(PORTAL_SRC);
+
+// Strip line and block comments so a mention in a comment never trips the guard.
+function stripComments(src: string): string {
+  return src
+    .replace(/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g, '')
+    .replace(/(^|[^:])\/\/.*$/gm, '$1');
+}
+
+// Resolve a relative or @/ import specifier to an absolute file path on disk.
+function resolveImport(fromFile: string, spec: string): string | null {
+  let base: string;
+  if (spec.startsWith('@/')) {
+    base = join(PORTAL_SRC, spec.slice(2));
+  } else if (spec.startsWith('.')) {
+    base = resolve(dirname(fromFile), spec);
+  } else {
+    return null; // package import, outside the portal src graph
+  }
+  for (const cand of [base, base + '.ts', base + '.tsx', join(base, 'index.ts'), join(base, 'index.tsx')]) {
+    try {
+      if (statSync(cand).isFile()) return cand;
+    } catch {
+      // not this candidate
+    }
+  }
+  return null;
+}
+
+function localImports(file: string): string[] {
+  const src = stripComments(readFileSync(file, 'utf8'));
+  const specs: string[] = [];
+  const re = /\b(?:import|export)\b[^'"`]*?from\s*['"]([^'"]+)['"]/g;
+  let m: RegExpExecArray | null;
+  while ((m = re.exec(src)) !== null) specs.push(m[1]);
+  // bare side-effect imports: import '...'
+  const re2 = /\bimport\s*['"]([^'"]+)['"]/g;
+  while ((m = re2.exec(src)) !== null) specs.push(m[1]);
+  return specs
+    .map((s) => resolveImport(file, s))
+    .filter((p): p is string => p !== null);
+}
+
+function isClientFile(file: string): boolean {
+  const head = stripComments(readFileSync(file, 'utf8')).slice(0, 400);
+  return /^\s*['"]use client['"]/m.test(head);
+}
+
+describe('platform-admin is server side only (import graph)', () => {
+  it('no browser-reachable module imports platform-admin', () => {
+    const clientRoots = ALL_FILES.filter(isClientFile);
+    // Transitive closure of local imports from every client root.
+    const reached = new Set<string>();
+    const stack = [...clientRoots];
+    while (stack.length) {
+      const f = stack.pop()!;
+      if (reached.has(f)) continue;
+      reached.add(f);
+      for (const dep of localImports(f)) {
+        if (!reached.has(dep)) stack.push(dep);
+      }
+    }
+    const offenders = [...reached].filter((f) =>
+      localImports(f).includes(PLATFORM_ADMIN),
+    );
+    expect(offenders, `browser-reachable files importing platform-admin:\n${offenders.join('\n')}`).toEqual([]);
+  });
+});
+
+describe('platform-admin reads customer data only, never portal tables', () => {
+  // A portal-owned table name. The check below only flags one of these when it is
+  // read THROUGH the platform client, not merely because the name appears in a
+  // file that also, legitimately, holds a platform client for a customer read.
+  const PORTAL_TABLE = '(?:portal_[a-z_]+|founder_[a-z_]+|health_history|infra_cost_history|mrr_snapshots|risk_register|rd_log|headcount_plan|sales_pipeline|agent_[a-z_]+|calendar_events|cost_receipts|document_log|event_ingestion_log|infra_subscriptions|regulation_updates|approval_queue)';
+
--8<-- END CHUNK 8/12 --8<--

---

### #138 · KIRO · 2026-11-01 15:25 UTC

PATCH 9/12
--8<-- BEGIN CHUNK 9/12 --8<--
+  it('no portal-owned table is read THROUGH the platform client', () => {
+    const importers = ALL_FILES.filter(
+      (f) => localImports(f).includes(PLATFORM_ADMIN),
+    );
+    const offenders: string[] = [];
+    for (const f of importers) {
+      const src = stripComments(readFileSync(f, 'utf8'));
+      // Find the variable(s) that hold a platform client: `const X = getPlatformAdmin()`.
+      const vars = new Set<string>();
+      const vre = /\b(?:const|let|var)\s+([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)\s*=\s*getPlatformAdmin\s*\(/g;
+      let vm: RegExpExecArray | null;
+      while ((vm = vre.exec(src)) !== null) vars.add(vm[1]);
+      // Also catch a direct chained call getPlatformAdmin().from('portal_...').
+      const directChain = new RegExp(
+        `getPlatformAdmin\\s*\\(\\s*\\)\\s*\\.from\\(\\s*['"\`]${PORTAL_TABLE}['"\`]`,
+        'g',
+      );
+      if (directChain.test(src)) {
+        offenders.push(`${f}: getPlatformAdmin().from(portal table)`);
+      }
+      // For each platform-client variable, flag <var>.from('portal_...').
+      for (const v of vars) {
+        const viaVar = new RegExp(
+          `\\b${v}\\s*\\.from\\(\\s*['"\`]${PORTAL_TABLE}['"\`]`,
+          'g',
+        );
+        const hits = src.match(viaVar);
+        if (hits) offenders.push(`${f}: ${v}.from(...) on a portal table`);
+      }
+    }
+    expect(
+      offenders,
+      `portal tables read through the platform client:\n${offenders.join('\n')}`,
+    ).toEqual([]);
+  });
+});

+//
+// After the portal moves to its own Supabase project (upxwdxhqzdsjnpsftsfb), the
+// portal's own clients (admin.ts, server.ts, browser.ts) point at the PORTAL
+// project. But the portal still reads some CUSTOMER data that lives in the
+// platform project (organisations, profiles, product_subscriptions,
+// subscriptions) and the platform table ai_model_registry. Those reads go
+// through THIS client, never the portal client.
+//
+// SERVER SIDE ONLY. This holds the platform service role key, which must never
+// reach the browser bundle. The import-graph guard
+// (src/lib/supabase/__tests__/platform-admin-is-server-only.test.ts) fails the
+// build if any browser-reachable module imports this file. There is deliberately
+// no 'use client' anywhere in its import chain.
+//
+// It reads a SEPARATE pair of variables from the portal's own, so the two
+// connections can never be confused and the portal default pair is free to point
+// at the new project:
+//   PLATFORM_SUPABASE_URL
+//   PLATFORM_SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY
+// Both are set for the switch-over (see the env list in DESIGN/cutover notes).
+// There is no fallback to NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL: an unset platform variable
+// must fail loudly rather than silently read the portal project, which would
+// return nothing for a customer query and look like missing data.
+import { createClient, type SupabaseClientOptions } from '@supabase/supabase-js';
+
+export const PLATFORM_SUPABASE_URL_VAR = 'PLATFORM_SUPABASE_URL';
+export const PLATFORM_SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY_VAR = '<removed>';
+
+/**
+ * Service-role client bound to the PLATFORM project. Use ONLY for customer data
+ * the portal reads (organisations, profiles, product_subscriptions,
+ * subscriptions) and ai_model_registry. Never for portal_* tables, and never
+ * from a client component.
+ *
+ * Throws if the platform variables are unset, deliberately: a customer read that
+ * silently hit the portal project would return an empty result and be mistaken
+ * for missing data.
+ */
+export function getPlatformAdmin() {
+  const url = (process.env[PLATFORM_SUPABASE_URL_VAR] ?? '').trim();
+  const key = <removed> ?? '').trim();
+  if (!url || !key) {
+    const missing = [
+      url ? null : PLATFORM_SUPABASE_URL_VAR,
+      key ? null : PLATFORM_SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY_VAR,
+    ]
+      .filter((n): n is string => n !== null)
+      .join(' and ');
+    throw new Error(
+      `The platform connection needs ${missing}. It is NOT inherited from the ` +
+        'portal Supabase variables, so an unset value fails here rather than ' +
+        'reading the portal project in place of the platform project.',
+    );
+  }
+  const authOptions: NonNullable<SupabaseClientOptions<'public'>['auth']> = {
+    autoRefreshToken: false,
+    persistSession: false,
+  };
+  return createClient(url, key, { auth: authOptions });
+}
--

From a83ac7b887aef3e3ca3bca0b6835956bb88e6ad3 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Velstrian Tenderworks <platform@velstrian.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 14:36:10 +0000
Subject: [PATCH 13/19] R29-PORTAL-OWN-SUPABASE-01: step 3 storage buckets
 migration + object-copy script

9100_storage_buckets.sql creates portal-receipts and portal-documents with verbatim config and the 4 portal_documents storage.objects policies, applied to the portal project. copy_portal_storage.py (owner-run) moves the 5 portal-receipts object bytes via the Storage API, env keys only, dry run then --apply, sha256 compare per object, counts/paths only.
---
 .../copy_portal_storage.py                    | 120 ++++++++++++++++++
 .../migrations/9100_storage_buckets.sql       |  44 +++++++
 2 files changed, 164 insertions(+)
 create mode 100644 docs/release-2.9/portal-own-supabase/copy_portal_storage.py
 create mode 100644 supabase/portal/migrations/9100_storage_buckets.sql

diff --git a/docs/release-2.9/portal-own-supabase/copy_portal_storage.py b/docs/release-2.9/portal-own-supabase/copy_portal_storage.py
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..ffa4a1b29
--- /dev/null
+++ b/docs/release-2.9/portal-own-supabase/copy_portal_storage.py
@@ -0,0 +1,120 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+# R29-PORTAL-OWN-SUPABASE-01 step 3 (storage): copy the portal-receipts storage
+# objects from the platform project to the new portal project, credential-safe.
+#
+# WHO RUNS THIS: the owner, on the owner's machine. Neither AI holds the service
+# keys. This script reads them ONLY from environment variables and never prints,
+# logs or writes them.
+#
+#   PLATFORM_SUPABASE_URL              https://<platform-ref>.supabase.co
+#   PLATFORM_SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY platform service-role key (read)
+#   PORTAL_SUPABASE_URL                https://upxwdxhqzdsjnpsftsfb.supabase.co
+#   PORTAL_SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY   portal service-role key (write)
+#
+# The two buckets (portal-receipts, portal-documents) and their RLS policies are
+# already created by migration 9100_storage_buckets.sql, so this script only
+# moves the object BYTES. portal-documents has 0 objects, so only the 5
+# portal-receipts objects move (265,615 bytes total, measured 2026-11-01).
+#
+# For each object it downloads from the source bucket, uploads to the target
+# bucket at the SAME path with the SAME content-type, and compares the sha256 of
+# the source bytes against the sha256 of the bytes read back from the target. It
+# prints COUNTS and per-object PATH + sha-match only, never the bytes. Default is
+# a dry run (lists what would copy). --apply performs the upload. Re-runnable:
+# upsert is used, and a path already present with a matching sha is reported and
+# skipped.
+#
+# Requires: Python 3, supabase (supabase-py v2).  pip install supabase
+#
+# Usage:
+#   python copy_portal_storage.py          # dry run: list source objects, counts
+#   python copy_portal_storage.py --apply  # download from platform, upload to portal, verify sha256
+
+import hashlib
+import os
+import sys
+
+try:
+    from supabase import create_client
+except ImportError:
+    sys.exit("supabase-py is required: pip install supabase")
+
+BUCKETS = ["portal-receipts", "portal-documents"]
+
+
+def client(url_var, key_var):
+    url = (os.environ.get(url_var) or "").strip()
+    key = <removed> or "").strip()
+    if not url or not key:
+        sys.exit(f"Set {url_var} and {key_var} in the environment. "
+                 "They are never read from anywhere else and never printed.")
+    return create_client(url, key)
+
+
+def list_objects(sb, bucket):
+    # Supabase storage list is per-prefix; receipts are stored flat or under a
+    # small set of prefixes. Walk one level of folders to be safe.
+    out = []
+    root = sb.storage.from_(bucket).list("", {"limit": 1000})
+    for entry in root:
+        name = entry.get("name")
+        if name is None:
+            continue
+        # A folder entry has no id/metadata; recurse one level.
+        if entry.get("id") is None:
+            for child in sb.storage.from_(bucket).list(name, {"limit": 1000}):
+                cn = child.get("name")
+                if cn:
+                    out.append(f"{name}/{cn}")
+        else:
+            out.append(name)
+    return out
+
+
+def main():
+    apply = "--apply" in sys.argv[1:]
+
+    src = client("PLATFORM_SUPABASE_URL", "PLATFORM_SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY")
+    dst = client("PORTAL_SUPABASE_URL", "PORTAL_SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY")
+
+    grand_total = 0
+    mismatches = []
+    for bucket in BUCKETS:
+        paths = list_objects(src, bucket)
+        print(f"bucket {bucket}: {len(paths)} source objects")
+        grand_total += len(paths)
+        if not apply:
+            for p in paths:
+                print(f"  would copy: {p}")
+            continue
+
+        for p in paths:
+            data = src.storage.from_(bucket).download(p)
+            src_sha = hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
+            # Infer content type from the source object metadata where possible;
+            # fall back to octet-stream. upsert so a rerun overwrites cleanly.
+            try:
+                dst.storage.from_(bucket).upload(
+                    p, data, {"contentType": "application/octet-stream", "upsert": "true"}
+                )
+            except Exception as exc:  # already exists without upsert support, etc.
+                # Surface the path, never the bytes.
+                print(f"  upload note for {p}: {type(exc).__name__}")
+            back = dst.storage.from_(bucket).download(p)
+            dst_sha = hashlib.sha256(back).hexdigest()
+            ok = src_sha == dst_sha
+            print(f"  {p}: sha256 {'match' if ok else 'MISMATCH'}")
+            if not ok:
+                mismatches.append(p)
+
+    print(f"total source objects across buckets: {grand_total}")
+    if apply:
+        if mismatches:
+            sys.exit("sha256 MISMATCH on: " + ", ".join(mismatches))
+        print("APPLIED. Every copied object's sha256 matches the source.")
+    else:
+        print("DRY RUN. No objects copied. Re-run with --apply to perform the copy.")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()
diff --git a/supabase/portal/migrations/9100_storage_buckets.sql b/supabase/portal/migrations/9100_storage_buckets.sql
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..35f347d55
--- /dev/null
+++ b/supabase/portal/migrations/9100_storage_buckets.sql
@@ -0,0 +1,44 @@
+-- 9100_storage_buckets.sql
+-- R29-PORTAL-OWN-SUPABASE-01 step 3 (storage): the two portal storage buckets and
+-- their storage.objects RLS policies, reproduced from the live platform catalog.
+-- The object BYTES are copied separately by the owner-run copy_portal_storage.py
+-- (the bytes live in the storage backend, not in the database).
+--
+-- portal-receipts has NO storage.objects policy (service-role only, RLS bypassed).
+-- portal-documents has four policies gated on private.portal_role_for_current_user(),
+-- which already exists on this project from 0001_prereqs.sql.
+--
+-- Bucket config is verbatim from storage.buckets on the platform project:
+--   portal-documents: private, 50 MB limit, office + pdf + html + markdown mime types
+--   portal-receipts:  private, no size limit, no mime restriction
+
+INSERT INTO storage.buckets (id, name, public, file_size_limit, allowed_mime_types)
+VALUES
+  ('portal-documents', 'portal-documents', false, 52428800, ARRAY[
+     'application/pdf',
+     'application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document',
+     'application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.presentationml.presentation',
+     'application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet',
+     'text/html',
+     'text/markdown'
+   ]),
+  ('portal-receipts', 'portal-receipts', false, NULL, NULL)
+ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING;
+
+-- storage.objects policies for portal-documents (verbatim from pg_policies).
+CREATE POLICY "portal_documents_storage_select" ON storage.objects
+  FOR SELECT TO authenticated
+  USING ((bucket_id = 'portal-documents'::text) AND (private.portal_role_for_current_user() = ANY (ARRAY['founder'::text, 'admin'::text, 'security'::text, 'engineer'::text, 'viewer'::text])));
+
+CREATE POLICY "portal_documents_storage_insert" ON storage.objects
+  FOR INSERT TO authenticated
+  WITH CHECK ((bucket_id = 'portal-documents'::text) AND (private.portal_role_for_current_user() = ANY (ARRAY['founder'::text, 'admin'::text, 'engineer'::text])));
+
+CREATE POLICY "portal_documents_storage_update" ON storage.objects
+  FOR UPDATE TO authenticated
+  USING ((bucket_id = 'portal-documents'::text) AND (private.portal_role_for_current_user() = ANY (ARRAY['founder'::text, 'admin'::text, 'engineer'::text])))
+  WITH CHECK ((bucket_id = 'portal-documents'::text) AND (private.portal_role_for_current_user() = ANY (ARRAY['founder'::text, 'admin'::text, 'engineer'::text])));
+
+CREATE POLICY "portal_documents_storage_delete" ON storage.objects
+  FOR DELETE TO authenticated
+  USING ((bucket_id = 'portal-documents'::text) AND (private.portal_role_for_current_user() = ANY (ARRAY['founder'::text, 'admin'::text, 'engineer'::text])));
--

+
+
+## 9. Switch-over runbook
+
+Added 2026-11-01. This is the ordered cutover. Every step here is an OWNER or DRIVER
+action (env changes, promote, deploy). Kiro does not run any of it. Staging first, prove it,
+then production. Rollback at every stage is reverting the env vars and re-promoting, because the
+old platform-project tables are left in place until a week after a clean production switch.
+
+### Preconditions (all already done on the branch unless noted)
+- Schema (42 tables), auth copy (4 founders), the 10 auth FKs, the data copy, and the 5 storage
+  objects are all present on `upxwdxhqzdsjnpsftsfb`. Verify counts before switching.
+- Founder 5's auth account exists on the new project (owner dashboard invite, accepted).
+- The step 4 code (`getPlatformAdmin`) is merged into the release flow by the driver.
+- Owner has enabled Turnstile in the new project's Auth Attack Protection (captcha, decision a).
+
+### Env vars on the portal Vercel project (set by the owner/driver, STAGING environment first)
+Repoint the portal's own connection to the NEW project, and add the platform connection:
+
+| Variable | New value | Why |
+|---|---|---|
+| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` | the new portal project URL | portal sign-in and portal_* tables |
+| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` | new portal publishable key | browser portal client |
+| `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` | new portal secret key | server portal admin client |
+| `PLATFORM_SUPABASE_URL` | the platform project URL (unchanged target) | `getPlatformAdmin()` customer reads |
+| `PLATFORM_SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` | platform secret key | `getPlatformAdmin()` customer reads |
+| `PORTAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` | SAME value as today | `portal_integrations` ciphertext stays readable |
+
+Values are pasted in the Vercel/Supabase dashboards by the owner. No value appears in code, in
+git, or in the channel. A Vercel env change applies only on the next build, so each change is
+paired with a promote.
+
+### Order
+1. Set the six variables on the portal Vercel project, STAGING environment.
+2. `pnpm staging:promote --project portal` (driver). Never a git deploy.
+3. Prove staging-portal: each founder signs in with password + TOTP, registers a fresh passkey on
+   the velstrian host, and the post-switch checks below pass.
+4. Owner approves production. Set the same six variables on the production environment.
+5. `pnpm prod:promote` for the portal, with the owner's approval text naming the sha (driver).
+6. Prove production with the same checks.
+7. Only after a week of the portal running clean on the new project: the platform-side drop of the
+   42 moved tables, plus the guard/fixture/types updates, in one driver commit (separate row).
+
+### Rollback
+At any stage before step 7, revert the portal Vercel variables to the platform project values and
+re-promote. The new project is left intact (no drop), so a revert is a pure env change. Because the
--8<-- END CHUNK 9/12 --8<--

It immediately surfaced 4 more customer tables the portal reads cross-project (tenant_datasource_catalog, beta_invites, revoked_tokens, agency_client_limits), each verified present on platform and absent on portal, and already correctly on the platform client. Guard re-proven green (20 importers, 0 offenders both checks). platform-admin.ts already has import 'server-only'. From da99943f98da854852f62b558c65eb7fda81aacd Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001

Subject: [PATCH 17/19] R29-PORTAL-OWN-SUPABASE-01: fix review findings 9,
 3-sibling, 10

Finding 9 (storage): copy_portal_storage.py now reads each object's real content type from source metadata (not octet-stream), implements a real rerun skip (download target, skip when sha256 already matches), and states the one-level-list depth limit. Finding 3-sibling (trial-end-reversible.ts): documented that assertNotProduction must be given the PLATFORM url and that these helpers have no runtime caller (staging tests/harnesses only), so the portal-vs-platform url concern is a forward contract. Finding 10 (runbook): rollback now specifies freeze writes, delta copy back or accept loss, keep the 42 platform tables undropped for the week, and a hard gate that the drops wait for the 3 HIGH fixes plus a passing staging walk.

  * production throws before it can touch a row. Never bypassable by a caller

  * it throws.
+ *

  */

   const ref = projectRefFromSupabaseUrl(supabaseUrl);

 ### Rollback
 At any stage before step 7, revert the portal Vercel variables to the platform project values and
 re-promote. The new project is left intact (no drop), so a revert is a pure env change. Because the
-move copied data rather than moving it, the platform tables are still authoritative until step 7,
-so a rollback loses only writes made against the new project during the trial window (founders are
-told to hold off non-trivial portal writes during the staging window).
+move copied data rather than moving it, the platform tables are still authoritative until step 7.
+
+What a rollback does to writes made against the new project during the live window (finding 10):
+- Those writes (new portal_* rows, new receipts) exist ONLY on the new project. A plain env revert
+  does not carry them back to the platform tables, so they would be lost on the portal once it
+  points at platform again.
+- So the rollback procedure is, in order: (a) FREEZE portal writes (put the portal in the
+  maintenance/read-only state or stop its crons), (b) run a final DELTA copy BACK from the new
+  project to the platform tables with copy_portal_data.py pointed the other way and
+  --allow-nonempty (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING tops up only the new rows), or explicitly ACCEPT the
+  loss of the window's writes and say so to the owner, then (c) revert the env and re-promote.
+- The 42 moved tables on the platform project stay UNDROPPED until at least a week after a clean
+  production switch, so this back-copy target always exists during the risk window.
+
+Hard gate on the drops (step 7): the platform-side drop of the 42 tables and the guard/fixture/type
+updates MUST NOT run until all three HIGH review findings (1 customer global logout, 2 ai_calls, 3
+onboarding production gate) are fixed AND a full staging walk of the portal on the new project has
+passed (sign in, activity feed, workflows, integrations, a customer page proving getPlatformAdmin).
 
 ### Post-switch checks (run on each environment after its promote)
 - Sign in: password, then TOTP challenge, then a freshly registered passkey. All succeed.

+// [R29-PORTAL-OWN-SUPABASE-01] Guard for the Test User Purge route (review
+// finding 8). The purge lists and deletes CUSTOMER auth users on the PLATFORM
+// project. It must NEVER touch portal_users (the founders' own directory): a
+// purge that reached portal_users under a portal RBAC session could delete an
+// operator. This asserts, from the source, that the route uses the platform
+// connection and references no portal-owned table.
+//
+// Kept SEPARATE from route.test.ts (the [R271-PORTAL-D22] Products-column guard)
+// so both run, this one asserts the connection and table set, that one asserts
+// the wire format.
+
+import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
+import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
+import { resolve } from 'node:path';
+
+const ROUTE = resolve(__dirname, 'route.ts');
+
+function stripComments(src: string): string {
+  return src
+    .replace(/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g, '')
+    .replace(/(^|[^:])\/\/.*$/gm, '$1');
+}
+
+describe('users/list purge touches only customer data, never portal_users', () => {
+  const src = stripComments(readFileSync(ROUTE, 'utf8'));
+
+  it('uses the platform connection (getPlatformAdmin), not the portal admin client', () => {
+    expect(src).toMatch(/getPlatformAdmin/);
+    expect(src).not.toMatch(/from '@\/lib\/supabase\/admin'/);
+    expect(src).not.toMatch(/createAdminClient/);
+  });
+
+  it('references no portal-owned table', () => {
+    const portalTable = /\.from\(\s*['"`](portal_[a-z_]+|founder_[a-z_]+|health_history|infra_cost_history|mrr_snapshots|risk_register|rd_log|headcount_plan|agent_[a-z_]+|calendar_events|cost_receipts|document_log|event_ingestion_log|infra_subscriptions|regulation_updates)['"`]/g;
+    const hits = src.match(portalTable);
+    expect(hits, `portal tables referenced by the purge route: ${hits?.join(', ')}`).toBeNull();
+    expect(src).not.toMatch(/portal_users/);
+  });
+
+  it('only reads the customer tables it needs (profiles, organisations) and lists auth users', () => {
+    expect(src).toMatch(/\.from\(\s*['"`]profiles['"`]/);
+    expect(src).toMatch(/\.from\(\s*['"`]organisations['"`]/);
+    expect(src).toMatch(/auth\.admin\.listUsers/);
+  });
+});

+}) {
+  const failing = new Set(opts.failing ?? []);

From f8d270f5b29ec5fad6cc321c94bdbc91e0699fe8 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Velstrian Tenderworks <platform@velstrian.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 00:01:12 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] R29-PORTAL-OWN-SUPABASE-01: step 4 two connections, customer
 reads via getPlatformAdmin + import-graph guard

New apps/portal/src/lib/supabase/platform-admin.ts getPlatformAdmin() (server-side only, reads PLATFORM_SUPABASE_URL/PLATFORM_SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, no fallback to the portal vars). 16 call sites that read customer tables (organisations, profiles, product_subscriptions, subscriptions) and ai_model_registry now use it; the two trial helpers are client-agnostic and their callers pass the platform client. The portal's own clients still read the portal vars, which point at the new project after the env switch. New import-graph guard fails if any browser-reachable module imports platform-admin, or if a portal table is read through the platform client; red-then-green proven.
